description: A numeric chip that increases and decreases by dragging horizontally and accepts typed input; values are displayed with Persian digits.
interactionNotes: Drag on the chip to change the number; outside the range, the chip tilts a little and springs back when you let go. `Shift` gives a coarse jump and `Alt` a fine adjustment. Click the number and type — both Persian and Latin digits are read. `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` move one step, `PageUp`/`PageDown` ten steps, and `Home`/`End` to either end of the range; `Escape` cancels mid-drag.

props.label: Label next to the number.
props.suffix: Unit next to the number; leave it empty to have none.
props.value: Controlled value; pass it to control the value yourself.
props.step: Size of each step; the number of decimal places comes from it too.
props.size: Height, font size, radius and the chip's width.
props.sensitivity: How many pixels of dragging count as one `step`; a lower number means faster.
props.rubberReach: How many percent of the range the spring can reach outside `min`/`max`.
props.returnDuration: Duration of the return into the range after release.
props.showDelta: The floating delta chip above the indicator.
props.showDirty: A ring around the chip when the value differs from `defaultValue`.
props.showFill: The colored fill that shows the size of the value.
props.accent: Accent color — the value fill, the delta chip and the changed ring.
props.onChange: On every value change — even mid-drag.
props.onCommit: Only when the drag has ended and the value actually changed.
props.className: Extra class for the root element.

tips: Use `onCommit` for heavy work and `onChange` for live display — keep that separation. `onChange` is called on every drag frame.
The input reads both Persian and Latin digits. Persian keyboards send Persian digits and a raw `parseFloat` reads them as `NaN`; here both work the same.
If you set `min` and `max` to the same number, the range becomes zero and the rubber-band stretch turns off — the component doesn't break, it just loses its spring.
Label and unit are UI, not data — they are shown on the chip itself and announced in `aria-valuetext`. So keep them Persian.
The value is **displayed** with Persian digits, but `aria-valuenow` stays a Latin number — the same thing assistive technology reads.
